title: 2026-04-23 — COO — Opryshko Bohdan — Crypto Market Recovery, Ukraine Lessons, And Staking Resilience: Bohdan Opryshko On Geopolitics
text:

As soon as we have some geopolitical crisis, some guys just decided to stake more. So I stake today, but I started generating rewards only in the 60 days because so many people wants to do that. So it's, like, extremely impossible. So that's why in this particular situation, for

So it means minus 30% of ETH, not in the market. So it means they have good possibility to, like, price goes up and people, like, want to buy more because it's a good, like, financial instrument. So it was not a huge line with the guys who was unstake or something. It was just a, it's normal. So it means that people don't want to unstake. They believe that they long-term players. And people want to buy a dip and stake more just because they see it's a good financial instrument for them on this, during this, let's say, bad market, not, like, not the bull market. Something like that.
[18:04] Bohdan Opryshko, Co-founder and COO at Everstake (company participant; testimony at recording): Interesting question. I guess it's, like, depends on a chain. Because if you're talking about Bitcoin, Ethereum, totally different. Like, we already talk with Ethereum, it's like around 30, 40% of the whole market. So it means that if 30% of it stayed, people cannot go back. So we don't see some huge movements during this weeks. If you're talking about Bitcoins, for example, it's totally different stuff becauseright now we have ETFs. Yeah, and, like, why after iron crisis, why price goes back to 70,000? Just because all this institutional, they just decided buy the dip. It was a perfect time for them. So that's why this geopolitical crisis was not that bad for crypto market during these months. And we even check some data that BlackRock ETFs just recorded approximately 260 million just in a couple of days. Inflows, I mean, just in a couple of days, just because it was a good time to buy it. So answering your question, I guess on-chain activity makes more sense because people try somehow to respond what's happening outside of the crypto market because it's anyway, it's correlates. So something like that.
[20:03] Bohdan Opryshko, Co-founder and COO at Everstake (company participant; testimony at recording): I guess four years ago, when we had invasion in Ukraine, there is no institutional in crypto. Of course, there is some, but not that much likeright now. Especially after all this new laws that, like, we support crypto in US, like, this is more become, like, green zone, not a gray zone. It's like some additional benchmark for institutionals to come in. When I am on a conference, like, for example, in 2022, and I met some guys from bank and started saying that I am work from crypto, they look at me like an evil and said, okay, bye, and just go away. Sometimes just disappear. When I amright now on a conference and want to talk with some guys from banks and saying their freedom, they start doing like, okay, tell me more. Because sooner or later, we, like a bank, have to acquire validator or we, like a bank, have to set up our own validator because we have, like, a bank, we have to somehow manage our customers' money. And it's not only, like, dollar, euro or something. It's going to be, like, Ethereum, Bitcoin, and others. So that's why I seeright now, past all these four years,right now we are more on a green zone. And at that time, we don't have a Bitcoin ETF, Ethereum ETF. That's whyright now it's awesome. At that time, we don't have Ethereum staking. Right now we have Ethereum staking. So people cannot so easy go away because they are talking for stated and they are for long-term here. And then for us, like, for us, for a company like Everstake, it's, of course, it's much, much betterright now because when I talk with some guys, they look at us like some sort of outside some financial institution, like, who can help with the operation, who can help with the infrastructure and so on. At that time, it was something like, oh, I even don't want to talk with you because cryp

[22:57] Bohdan Opryshko, Co-founder and COO at Everstake (company participant; testimony at recording): Like, everything correlated very well together. So I'm dead sure that if something might happen with any other countries or any other, like, place in the world, crypto definitely will respond. We also saw some data that as soon as all this crisis of iron happened, it was some, like, huge withdrawals of Iranians exchange, crypto exchange to some private wallets. But because everything that we're doing have to continue and we have to show, like, our credo in Everstake. We have to show that crypto is nothing bad. [0:18] Maria Belashova, Tezos Blockchain Manager at Everstake (company participant; testimony at recording): Thank you. I'm good, and I'm really glad to be here. Thank you.
[0:34] Maria Belashova, Tezos Blockchain Manager at Everstake (company participant; testimony at recording): Yeah. My personal journey into the world of crypto started, I think, 4 or 5 years ago, and I began my career in marketing. I also always had a passion for new technologies, and also I had one of my friends that worked in a blockchain startup, and he told me so many information about crypto, blockchain, how it works, and also I was really fascinated about the opportunities blockchain field could give to people. And I think it's like an innovation of the century. And I thought that I need to join the company, the blockchain company, and my first crypto job was at the crypto exchange. I worked as a marketer. And then, 2 years ago, I joined EverStake as blockchain manager. Blockchain manager's main responsibilities are to monitor the network upgrades and network use, different proposals, governance proposals, communicate with teams, with foundations, with influencers. Also it depends on the network. We posting, we creating different articles, guides, and educate people how to stake. We are developing different things, and I'm really happy to be here.
[2:59] Maria Belashova, Tezos Blockchain Manager at Everstake (company participant; testimony at recording): Yeah. EverStake is the biggest decentralized staking provider. Also we are the biggest retail validator. Now we have more than 735,000 users. And also we run 45, 46 years, we run more than 11,000 nodes across the 70-plus blockchains, including Tezos, Solana, Ethereum, Cosmos, Aptos, Polygon, etc. The most famous, yeah. And also we need different guidelines to select theright server for each specific blockchain, because there are different recommendations. And also I want to highlight that for the past 6 years, we are not only a validator, we also active investor in different blockchains, in different projects. Also we are developing different tools. For example, we have our RPC node for Solana named ExtraNode. It's also a separate team. We have different staking tools. Also we have our SDK. We creating dashboards, explorers for different blockchains, and we are developing in different fields now. Not only validating blockchains, but also other different things. And I think now we're something more than just a staking provider.
[5:39] Maria Belashova, Tezos Blockchain Manager at Everstake (company participant; testimony at recording): Yeah. Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. And also we have really great R&D and data science teams, because R&D, they are looking for new opportunities for us, for new projects. And every day they have a lot of calls, a lot of meetings to bring something new to EverStake, to have more partners, to have more networks, and also to employ more people, because we are bigger and bigger from year to year, and we are proud of it, yeah.
[6:37] Maria Belashova, Tezos Blockchain Manager at Everstake (company participant; testimony at recording): EverStake integrate Tezos in 2018, yeah, and we have been actively involved with Tezos from the very beginning. And this integration allowed users to stake their tokens, and we became Baker. And also by providing our infrastructure, EverStake users could delegate their XTZ and participate in the Tezos network consensus, and also in return they earn staking rewards. Now within the Tezos ecosystem, we are the first in the top by our total stake and voting power. And also we are the first by number of stakers and delegators. And it's not only numbers for us, it's the understanding about our weight in the ecosystem. We are an active participant here in all different governance proposals, in educational content, and we understand our voting power and that we could give different opinions and changes, for example, to the protocol, to its improvement. And governance decision, it's a really important thing for us, because we never vote like majority voted for this, and we voted also for this never, because we need to study carefully all changes and how it influence, especially on Bakers, on delegators, and what is the mood in the community. We also communicate with our delegators to understand, to understand their mood, how they like this proposal, this change, or no. And we discuss, we discuss all these changes internally with our team. Also our R&D department included in this conversation. And we need to study all pros and cons of each proposal to understand the future, the future of Tezos, the future, the future of us as Baker, and the future for delegators. And yeah, always our decision, they are, I think, well communicated, and because we need to understand the benefits for the ecosystem.
[10:23] Maria Belashova, Tezos Blockchain Manager at Everstake (company participant; testimony at recording): Yeah, sure. Staking is a process used in proof-of-stake networks, and the main goals are to secure the network, to validate transactions, and to produce new blocks. In staking, users, they stake, or in other words, they lock up their tokens to support the network and network operations. And in return, they receive rewards. Like for newcomers, we can compare it to like this bank deposit. It's maybe now it's not theright comparing, but the process and the main idea, we have like something the same. But in staking, no one will take your funds, and you have the full custody of your tokens. Of course, you need to be aware of scammers, because in blockchain it's so, so, so rare. And maybe if you join the crypto field, you need to watch all videos, all like, read a lot of information to be ready for different attacks, because it's, we have, because we have our Discord server, and often users come with, not questions, but with statements like, "Did they stole my tokens?" or "My wallet disappeared!" or something like that. And we try to educate our users, try to produce more articles, more threads on Twitter, and etc. But this situation are so rare. Yeah. And I think the main, the main benefits of staking crypto, of course it's passive income. It's the main goal for maybe everyone who come to staking as a user. It's full custody, as I told earlier, only you have access to your tokens, and no one could stake or unstake your tokens. Also with staking, you could support the project you like and contribute to the security of this project. And also you, by staking, you could do your, do the blockchain more resistant to different attacks. Also it's, the benefit is decentralization, because staking encourages a larger number of validators and delegators in the network, and it's promot
[13:07] Maria Belashova, Tezos Blockchain Manager at Everstake (company participant; testimony at recording): ing decentralization. And I think decentralization is the main goal and idea of many networks now, nowadays. And more validators and more delegators, they help to distribute the control of the network, and it really reduces the risk of centralization. And we could say that the blockchain could be more trustworthy for all users and for all participants. Also I think one of the benefits is decision making and governance participation, because if you're a staker, you also, in many networks, you could vote and participate in on-chain governance. For example, you could cast your vote for different upgrades, for different changes to the network, and you could influence the development of each project, or for example, different future changes. And it's very cool that you could be a part of the ecosystem, and you could be an active participant. I think it's so important to be the part of ecosystem you like, for example, and you could, you could do some change, some great changes for the project. Yeah. And about security, I could say that staking is very important, and it's, I think, the main idea, because staking incentivized honest behavior in the network, because validators, they are voted only for validating transaction correctly. And different, for example, misbehavior or failure, it can lead to penalties, like slashing. And slashing is like when a validator misbehave. In different networks, they have different rules, and for example, the 5-10% of stake could be slashed. But it depends on the network. Also staking deters attacks, because staking increases the cost of attacking the network, like 51% attack. And attackers, they need a significant portion of stake tokens, but it become more expensive. Also staking promotes decentralization, as I told earlier, more stakers and
[16:17] Maria Belashova, Tezos Blockchain Manager at Everstake (company participant; testimony at recording): more validators means more decentralized network. Also staking ensures reliable operations. Validators, they maintain high uptime and performance. And also I want to add that rewards are also connected with it, because in different network, your API level depends on the validators uptime. And the higher uptime, logically the higher rewards you receive. And also staking is a long-term commitment, because you're locking your tokens in, like, long-term success. It's also a great influence on the network you join, yeah.
[18:26] Maria Belashova, Tezos Blockchain Manager at Everstake (company participant; testimony at recording): Yeah. Yeah, you'reright.
[18:46] Maria Belashova, Tezos Blockchain Manager at Everstake (company participant; testimony at recording): Yeah, sure. The Paris upgrade introduced a new functionality for the ecosystem. It's staking. And also is a new role staker, because previously we had only Baker and delegator. And staking means that stakers contribute to the Baker's security deposit, but without transferring custody of their funds. In return, they receive staking rewards, but from the Tezos protocol, because in delegation, users receive rewards from Baker. And unlike delegation, staking stays funds frozen and also could be subject to slashing, because delegation is liquid delegation, and slashing, the status of funds are liquid. And also, also in staking, you receive your reward also immediately, and it's automatically added to your staking balance. But in delegation, the first rewards come in 10 days. Yeah. It's, I think, it's like the main basic difference, differences. Yeah, I think that's all, yeah.
[22:06] Maria Belashova, Tezos Blockchain Manager at Everstake (company participant; testimony at recording): Yeah.
[22:18] Maria Belashova, Tezos Blockchain Manager at Everstake (company participant; testimony at recording): Yeah.
